title: Benchmarking DNA Sequence Models for Causal Regulatory Variant Prediction in Human Genetics

nodes.text: TraitGym is a curated benchmark dataset of regulatory genetic variants known to be causal or strong candidates across 113 Mendelian and 83 complex traits, with carefully matched control variants, framing causal variant prediction as binary classification.
nodes.evidence: we present TraitGym, a curated dataset of regulatory genetic variants that are either known to be causal or are strong candidates across 113 Mendelian and 83 complex traits, along with carefully constructed control variants

nodes.text: Alignment-based models CADD and GPN-MSA compare favorably for Mendelian traits and complex disease traits.
nodes.evidence: alignment-based models CADD and GPN-MSA compare favorably for Mendelian traits and complex disease traits

nodes.text: Functional-genomics-supervised models Enformer and Borzoi perform better than alignment-based models for complex non-disease traits.
nodes.evidence: while functional-genomics-supervised models Enformer and Borzoi perform better for complex non-disease traits

nodes.text: Evo2 shows substantial performance gains with scale but still lags behind alignment-based models, struggling particularly with enhancer variants.
nodes.evidence: Evo2 shows substantial performance gains with scale, but still lags somewhat behind alignment-based models, struggling particularly with enhancer variants

nodes.text: TraitGym is the only benchmark of causal non-coding variant prediction covering both Mendelian and complex human traits, and the only framework to evaluate both the latest functional-genomics-supervised and self-supervised models alongside strong non-neural baselines.
nodes.evidence: TraitGym is the only benchmark of causal non-coding variant prediction for both Mendelian and complex human traits

nodes.text: Existing variant benchmarks (BEND, GV-Rep) draw from ClinVar which is highly skewed toward coding and splice region variants and establish inadequate baselines, e.g. lacking conservation-based models that are usually strong for this task.
nodes.evidence: expert-reviewed pathogenic variants in ClinVar are highly skewed towards coding and splice region variants ... Neither of these benchmarks establishes adequate baselines for this task

nodes.text: GPN-Promoter is a new genomic language model introduced here, trained on promoters of 434 animal species following the GPN objective and a ByteNet convolutional architecture, focusing on regulatory regions.
nodes.evidence: We introduce a new gLM, called GPN-Promoter, trained using the genomes of 434 animal species, following the training objective of GPN ... and the ByteNet convolutional architecture ... only trained on promoters

nodes.text: GPN-Promoter compares favorably with other alignment-free self-supervised language models.
nodes.evidence: demonstrate that it compares favorably with other alignment-free self-supervised language models

nodes.text: Putatively causal and control variants are matched 9-to-1 within each chromosome on consequence and TSS distance (plus MAF and LD score for complex traits), with Mendelian causal variants drawn from OMIM and complex-trait variants from UK BioBank fine-mapping (PIP > 0.9 positives, PIP < 0.01 controls).
nodes.evidence: we sampled 9 non-coding variants from the control set, matching chromosome, consequence, and distance to transcription start site (TSS). For complex traits, we additionally matched MAF and linkage disequilibrium (LD) score

nodes.text: Classification of variants is substantially harder for complex traits than Mendelian traits, but ensembling input and predicted features from different models yields consistent improvement.
nodes.evidence: The classification of variants is substantially harder for complex traits, but consistent improvement is observed by ensembling input and predicted features from different models

nodes.text: Mendelian-trait variants are relatively easier to predict than complex-trait variants because they have larger effects on gene expression and are subject to stronger purifying selection, the signals picked up by supervised and self-supervised models respectively.
nodes.evidence: variants affecting Mendelian traits have larger phenotypic effect sizes ... tend to have larger effects on gene expression ... and tend to be subject to stronger purifying selection

nodes.text: Models are evaluated both as zero-shot scores and via ridge logistic regression linear probing on extracted features, using leave-one-chromosome-out cross-validation with AUPRC (baseline 0.1) as the metric.
nodes.evidence: We evaluate zero-shot model scores as well as ridge logistic regression classifiers (linear probing) ... we calculate the area under the precision recall curve (AUPRC) for each chromosome
